was: Town of Pennington Gap municipal RV park at the Leeman Field fairgrounds, near the North Fork of the Powell River. 21 full-hookup (30/50-amp) sites, RVs to ~45 ft, plus tent camping along the river. Reservations (Campspot). The RV pads sit in the open fairground lot ~150-250 m from the river with no river view; only the tent area is near the water. --Claude
note: Town of Pennington Gap RV park at the Leeman Field fairgrounds, beside the historic Leeman Field park (a seasonal pool, and a greenway with trout-stocked fishing access) and near the Stone Mountain ATV trailhead.  The RV pads sit in the open fairground lot, 150-250 m from the North Fork of the Powell River and out of sight of it; tent camping is along the river.  The fairgrounds hold ATV drag races, riding competitions, a rodeo and the Lee County Fair on some summer weekends. --Claude

was: Wythe County park near 90-acre Rural Retreat Lake. ~72 sites - primitive/tent and 30/50-amp water+electric RV sites (rigs to ~42 ft), disc golf, seasonal pool. Mixed reservations (Campspot) and first-come, first-served. Campground phone is seasonal: 276-686-4331 (May-Sept) / 276-223-4517 (Oct-Apr). RV/hookup sites are wooded and set back from the lake (reached by trail/boat launch); they do not front or overlook the water. --Claude
note: Wythe County campground on 90-acre Rural Retreat Lake, in the woods and set back from the water, which is reached by a trail or the boat launch; no RV site fronts or overlooks the lake.  There is a boat ramp, shoreline fishing (a Virginia license or access permit is needed from age 17), a trout pond, hiking trails, a playground and picnic shelters, and a swimming pool, closed for the 2026 season; swimming in the lake isn't allowed.  A site holds 6 people at most, alcohol isn't allowed, and quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.  The campground's own phone is answered May to September; from October to April call 276-223-4517. --Claude

was: Doddridge County Park near West Union, by the North Bend Rail Trail. 24 RV slips (8 full-hookup asphalt 50/30-amp, 16 gravel water/electric, varying lengths) plus tent sites and yurts; reservations via Campspot. Borders Meathouse Fork Creek, but the creekside sites are the wooded tent sites (RV slips set back). --Claude
note: Doddridge County Park's campground near West Union, an access point to the North Bend Rail Trail, with tent sites and three yurts beside its 24 RV slips.  Eight slips are asphalt and have sewer hookups; the other 16 are gravel, and their depths vary.  The park borders Meathouse Fork, but the creekside sites are the wooded tent sites, and the RV slips sit back from the creek.  The camp office has a store and a covered deck with a fireplace and television, Wi-Fi reaches the first ten slips, and the park has a pool from late May to early September, trails, playgrounds and courts. --Claude

Most of the park is seasonal: 140 seasonal sites and 20 for short stays.  There is a swimming beach on the lake (no lifeguard), fishing, a basketball court, an ice-cream stand, a restaurant, a clubhouse and store and a playground, and fireworks light the lake on holiday weekends. --Claude

was: Riverside RV resort on the Suwannee River at Mayo, with RV sites, cabins, tent sites, pool complex and a natural spring; takes transient/nightly guests (daily RV rates ~$54-80). Reservable online via Campspot. Two areas: Primrose Park (family) and Key West Village (21+). Large sites (40x80+).
note: Riverside resort on 65 acres by the Suwannee River at Mayo, with lodging from cabins to lodge rooms and two RV areas: Primrose Park for families (sites 101-236) and Key West Village for adults 21 and over (sites 300-469).  Its RV sites are 40 by 80 ft or larger, some of them fenced for pets, and there are heated pools and hot tubs (open all year), dog parks, laundry and a pet wash; Wi-Fi reaches some areas.  Lower Rendezvous, a separate area, has tent sites, water and electric sites for RVs to 20 ft and nine 30-amp full-hookup sites for RVs to 28 ft, without Wi-Fi or cable.  Long-term stays are in the Key West section. --Claude

discounts.note: 10% off the daily rate for military, seniors 60 and over and Good Sam members, and a 2-night Passport America discount; booked by phone only, not on holiday weekends, one discount per visit.

facilities.note: Wi-Fi in some areas only, none in Lower Rendezvous.

was: Private RV park at the I-75/I-10 crossroads in Lake City. Nightly/transient (from ~$65) plus weekly/monthly; reservable online via Campspot. Full-hookup sites, laundry, restrooms/showers, cable & WiFi. On-site stocked fishing pond.
note: RV park just off I-10 at Lake City, under oaks, pines and magnolias, with pull-through sites, a heated saltwater pool, a stocked fishing pond, two fenced dog parks and a dog wash, a ninja obstacle course, a pavilion with a grill, a commercial kitchen and 24-hour laundry; cabins and park models are rented.  Pets may not be tied out, caged or fenced at the site. --Claude

was: Small full-hookup RV park (~20 concrete-slab sites) on Hwy 29 about 5 mi from Wiggins; 30/50-amp, picnic table & fire ring per site, laundry, showers, on-property fishing pond. No tent camping. Reservable online via Campspot.
note: Locally owned RV park on US 29 at Wiggins, about 35 miles from the Mississippi beaches and 30 from Hattiesburg, with back-in and pull-through sites, fishing in its pond and Hobbs Creek, four private bathrooms with showers, coin laundry, a multipurpose room with fitness equipment, walking trails, horseshoes and croquet.  An efficiency cabin is rented. --Claude

was: Big-rig-friendly RV park on the SE edge of St. Cloud; 102 sites incl 45 pull-throughs and 77 full-hookup (30/50-amp), heated pool, store, laundry, dump station, rally center. Open May-Oct. Reservable (Campspot). --Claude
note: Country campground 2 miles east of downtown St. Cloud, with large open and wooded sites; staff lead each arrival to its site by golf cart.  It has a lodge with a snack bar, groceries and RV supplies, propane, a pool, a laundromat, firewood (outside firewood isn't allowed) and a 2,800-square-foot rally center with a kitchen.  For most of the season the guests are seniors, retirees and RV clubs, joined on summer weekends by families. --Claude

was: City of Morris park on Pomme de Terre Lake; ~20+ shaded gravel water/electric sites (many near the water's edge) plus tent space; shower houses, disc golf, swimming/boating/fishing. Reservable (Campspot). --Claude
note: City of Morris campground on Pomme de Terre Lake, with water and electric sites, tent sites, restrooms and showers, a spray park, a disc golf course, a dock, canoeing, fishing and a playground.  The city shuts the park's water off in mid-October; camping continues without it. --Claude
